questions.passage: Botanist Ynes Mexia began collecting plants at age 55, yet her output was anything but ______: over thirteen years she gathered roughly 145,000 specimens, among them hundreds of species previously unknown to science.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
choices: modest
documented
celebrated
deliberate
questions.explanation: The colon introduces evidence of a huge output (145,000 specimens), so the text needs a word meaning the opposite of that: her output was anything but modest.

questions.passage:
A student studying city parks recorded the average number of bird species seen per visit in parks of different sizes.

Bird Species Observed in City Parks
Park sizeAverage species per visit
Under 2 hectares6
2–10 hectares11
Over 10 hectares19

The student concluded that larger parks tend to support a greater variety of bird species.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes data from the table that support the student's conclusion?
choices: Parks under 2 hectares had an average of 6 species per visit.
The average number of species per visit rose as park size increased.
Parks of 2–10 hectares had nearly twice as many species as parks over 10 hectares.
Every park in the study had at least 6 species per visit.
questions.explanation: The conclusion is about a trend across sizes. Only choice B describes that trend: 6 → 11 → 19 as parks get larger.

questions.passage: In 1968, Mexican chemist Mario Molina began studying chlorofluorocarbons ______ chemicals then common in refrigerators and spray cans. His research showed that they were damaging Earth's ozone layer.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: chlorofluorocarbons;
chlorofluorocarbons,
chlorofluorocarbons. These
chlorofluorocarbons and
questions.explanation: “chemicals then common in refrigerators…” renames chlorofluorocarbons, so it is set off with a comma.

questions.passage: For decades, scientists believed that octopuses lived solitary lives. ______ divers off the coast of Australia have observed groups of octopuses living together in dens and even interacting with one another.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Similarly,
Recently, however,
For example,
As a result,
questions.explanation: The second sentence contradicts the old belief, and the observation is new, so “Recently, however,” fits.

questions.passage: The town of Kamikatsu, Japan, sorts its waste into more than forty categories. Residents wash and separate their own trash and bring it to a central station, where it is recycled or reused. As a result, the town now recycles about 80 percent of its waste, far above the national average.
questions.stem: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
choices: Kamikatsu's detailed sorting system has led to an unusually high recycling rate.
Most towns in Japan recycle about 80 percent of their waste.
Residents of Kamikatsu dislike the town's waste system.
Kamikatsu plans to add more waste categories in the future.
questions.explanation: The text describes the sorting system and its result: a recycling rate far above average.

questions.passage: The collection of handwritten letters, which the museum acquired last spring, ______ the daily life of sailors in the 1800s.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
choices: describe
describes
are describing
have described
questions.explanation: The subject is the singular noun “collection,” so the verb must be singular: describes.

questions.passage: Many people assume that bees find flowers by sight and smell alone. Researchers have found, however, that bumblebees can also sense the weak electric fields that surround flowers. A flower that a bee has just visited carries a slightly different charge, which may tell the next bee that the nectar is already gone.
questions.stem: Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?
choices: It describes a common belief and then presents a finding that adds to it.
It explains a scientific method and then lists its limitations.
It compares two species of bees and then explains how they differ.
It presents a theory and then explains why most researchers reject it.
questions.explanation: The text starts with what “many people assume” and then gives research (“however”) showing that bees also sense electric fields.

questions.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:

  • The Great Wall of China is not a single wall.
  • It is a series of walls built over many centuries.
  • The best-known sections were built during the Ming dynasty (1368–1644).
  • The walls stretch more than 20,000 kilometers in total.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize the length of the Great Wall. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: The Great Wall of China is a series of walls rather than a single wall.
The best-known sections of the Great Wall were built during the Ming dynasty.
Built over many centuries, the walls that make up the Great Wall of China stretch more than 20,000 kilometers.
The Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644.
questions.explanation: Only choice C mentions the total length (more than 20,000 kilometers).

questions.stem: If \(3x + 7 = 22\), what is the value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7: \(3x = 15\). Divide by 3: \(x = 5\).

questions.stem:
\[x + y = 10\]\[x - y = 4\]

What is the value of \(x\) in the solution to the system of equations above?
questions.explanation: Add the equations: \(2x = 14\), so \(x = 7\).

questions.stem:
In right triangle \(ABC\), the legs have lengths 6 and 8.

What is the length of the hypotenuse?
A line in the \(xy\)-plane passes through the points \((2, 3)\) and \((6, 6)\). What is the slope of the line?
questions.explanation: Slope \(= \dfrac{6-3}{6-2} = \dfrac{3}{4}\). Entering 3/4 or .75 both receive credit.

questions.stem: A jacket originally priced at $80 is on sale for 25% off. What is the sale price of the jacket?
questions.explanation: 25% of 80 is 20, so the sale price is \(80 - 20 = 60\) dollars.

questions.stem: A car travels 150 miles in 2.5 hours at a constant speed. At this speed, how many miles will the car travel in 4 hours?
questions.explanation: Speed \(= 150 \div 2.5 = 60\) miles per hour, so in 4 hours it travels \(240\) miles.

questions.stem: A circle in the \(xy\)-plane has equation \((x - 2)^2 + (y + 3)^2 = 16\). What is the radius of the circle?
questions.explanation: The equation has the form \((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\), so \(r^2 = 16\) and \(r = 4\).

questions.stem: In a right triangle, \(\sin \theta = \dfrac{3}{5}\), where \(\theta\) is an acute angle. What is the value of \(\cos \theta\)?
questions.explanation: With opposite 3 and hypotenuse 5, the adjacent side is 4, so \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{4}{5}\).

questions.stem: The function \(P(t) = 200(1.05)^t\) gives the population of a town, in thousands, \(t\) years after 2020. Which of the following is the best interpretation of the number 1.05 in this context?
choices: The population increases by 1.05 thousand people each year.
The population increases by 5% each year.
The population in 2020 was 1.05 thousand.
The population increases by 105% each year.
questions.explanation: A growth factor of 1.05 means each year's population is 105% of the year before: a 5% increase per year.

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 6\). What are the zeros of \(f\)?
questions.explanation: \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x-2)(x-3)\), so the zeros are 2 and 3.
